subject: Risk & Compliance
title: Fiduciary Duty Explained
description: A 60-second lesson on Fiduciary Duty Explained.

hook.text: A director votes to approve a deal that benefits his own company. That's a breach of fiduciary duty.

buildup.text: Fiduciary duty requires directors and officers to act in the best interest of the company and its shareholders.

discovery.text: It includes duty of care (make informed decisions) and duty of loyalty (avoid conflicts of interest).

twist.text: The business judgment rule protects directors from lawsuits if they acted in good faith, even if outcomes are bad.

climax.text: Fiduciary duty is the legal backbone of governance. Break it, and shareholders can sue.

punchline.text: Act in their interest, not yours. That's the duty.

quiz.question: What does fiduciary duty require of directors?
options: Acting in the best interest of shareholders
